newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norsk Hydro awards Troll C oil contract.
newsitem.headline: Norsk Hydro awards Troll C oil contract.

text.p: Norwegian industrial giant Norsk Hydro ASA said on Tuesday it had award a contract for work on the semi-submersible steel Troll C oil platform to Norway's Umoe Haugesund AS.

The contract comprises a steel floater with a deck frame, process module, utility module and living quarters. The floating production unit (FPU) contract value was around 3.9 billion crowns, Norsk Hydro said in a statement.
Troll C will be used for the production of additional oil reserves from the Troll field.
Hydro said total recoverable reserves from Troll were estimated at 185 million cubic metres, or 1.2 billion barrels, of oil.
The Troll C platform will produce from the northern part of the Troll West gas province and will process the oil from six well groups totalling 32 wells.
The platform will have a production capacity of 125,000 barrels per day and is schedule to begin operation in September, 1999.
Norsk Hydro said it has selected Umoe Haugesund, based on the west coast of Norway, from three contractor groups headed by Umoe, Kvaerner ASA and Aker ASA.
Umoe's unit will have a total weight of 24,000 tonnes, of which the topside facilities for processing and living quarters amount to 15,000 tonnes.
The platform will be anchored in 300 metres of water. Tow out is scheduled for June 1999.
